groups.name: Research Framing
groups.description: Shape a research problem from broad context to a bounded, defensible contribution.

groups.name: Literature Writing
groups.description: Represent, compare, and synthesise scholarship while keeping claims attached to their sources.

groups.name: Argumentation
groups.description: Build a traceable academic argument with calibrated claims, distinctions, concessions, and implications.

groups.name: Thesis and Dissertation Writing
groups.description: Coordinate long-form research chapters so each section performs a clear role in the whole argument.

groups.name: Publication Writing
groups.description: Adapt research content to publication genres, editorial exchanges, and transparency statements.

groups.name: Scientific Study Framing
groups.description: Connect a scientific question to prior evidence, testable expectations, and a bounded contribution.

groups.name: Methods Writing
groups.description: Report how a study was designed, conducted, analysed, and governed with enough detail for appraisal.

groups.name: Results Writing
groups.description: Report observations and estimates precisely before moving to interpretation.

groups.name: Discussion Writing
groups.description: Interpret findings against design, uncertainty, prior literature, and plausible alternatives.

groups.name: Scientific Claim Control
groups.description: Match scientific wording to design, evidence strength, uncertainty, and scope.

groups.name: Paraphrasing
groups.description: Rewrite academic material by preserving meaning, attribution, quantities, and inferential force.

skills.name: Establishing a research context
skills.description: Practical guidance to place the study within a bounded scholarly, social, or practical setting, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Place the study within a bounded scholarly, social, or practical setting.
skills.example: Research on urban heat has increasingly examined how neighbourhood design shapes exposure during extreme temperatures.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Support field-level statements with relevant sources, and define any claimed gap by topic, population, setting, and search scope.

skills.name: Introducing a topic
skills.description: Practical guidance to name the central subject and orient the reader without making an unsupported importance claim, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Name the central subject and orient the reader without making an unsupported importance claim.
skills.example: This article examines how community archives represent periods of forced migration.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Support field-level statements with relevant sources, and define any claimed gap by topic, population, setting, and search scope.

skills.name: Establishing significance
skills.description: Practical guidance to explain why a problem, question, or setting deserves attention for a stated audience, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Explain why a problem, question, or setting deserves attention for a stated audience.
skills.example: Reliable flood warnings matter because delayed alerts can narrow the time available for evacuation.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Support field-level statements with relevant sources, and define any claimed gap by topic, population, setting, and search scope.

skills.name: Defining a research problem
skills.description: Practical guidance to turn a broad concern into a specific condition that research can investigate, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Turn a broad concern into a specific condition that research can investigate.
skills.example: Existing battery tests do not capture performance loss under rapidly changing ambient temperatures.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Support field-level statements with relevant sources, and define any claimed gap by topic, population, setting, and search scope.

skills.name: Identifying a research gap
skills.description: Practical guidance to identify a bounded unanswered question rather than claiming that no research exists, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Identify a bounded unanswered question rather than claiming that no research exists.
skills.example: Although household energy use is well documented, its hour-by-hour response to heat alerts remains unclear.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Support field-level statements with relevant sources, and define any claimed gap by topic, population, setting, and search scope.

skills.name: Stating research aims
skills.description: Practical guidance to state the intended analytical, empirical, or conceptual outcome of the study, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: State the intended analytical, empirical, or conceptual outcome of the study.
skills.example: This study aims to estimate how travel time changes after bus-priority measures are introduced.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Support field-level statements with relevant sources, and define any claimed gap by topic, population, setting, and search scope.

skills.name: Writing research questions
skills.description: Practical guidance to formulate a focused question whose terms can be answered by the proposed evidence, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Formulate a focused question whose terms can be answered by the proposed evidence.
skills.example: We ask whether access to shaded public space differs across neighbourhood income levels.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Support field-level statements with relevant sources, and define any claimed gap by topic, population, setting, and search scope.

skills.name: Stating hypotheses
skills.description: Practical guidance to express a testable expectation and identify the relationship or difference being predicted, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Express a testable expectation and identify the relationship or difference being predicted.
skills.example: We hypothesise that seedlings exposed to intermittent drought will recover more slowly than continuously watered controls.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Support field-level statements with relevant sources, and define any claimed gap by topic, population, setting, and search scope.

skills.name: Describing scope
skills.description: Practical guidance to set explicit boundaries for population, place, period, material, or inference, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Set explicit boundaries for population, place, period, material, or inference.
skills.example: The analysis is limited to first-year students enrolled at three public universities between 2022 and 2024.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Support field-level statements with relevant sources, and define any claimed gap by topic, population, setting, and search scope.

skills.name: Stating contributions
skills.description: Practical guidance to describe what the study adds empirically, conceptually, or methodologically, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Describe what the study adds empirically, conceptually, or methodologically.
skills.example: The study contributes a district-level measure of cooling access that can be reproduced from open spatial data.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Support field-level statements with relevant sources, and define any claimed gap by topic, population, setting, and search scope.

skills.name: Describing novelty cautiously
skills.description: Practical guidance to describe a new feature without making an unverified priority or uniqueness claim, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Describe a new feature without making an unverified priority or uniqueness claim.
skills.example: To our knowledge, this analysis is among the first to compare these sensors under both laboratory and field conditions.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Support field-level statements with relevant sources, and define any claimed gap by topic, population, setting, and search scope.

skills.name: Introducing previous studies
skills.description: Practical guidance to bring prior research into the discussion with clear attribution and relevance, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Bring prior research into the discussion with clear attribution and relevance.
skills.example: Several longitudinal studies have linked stable housing with improved school attendance.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep each proposition attached to supporting citations, and distinguish source claims from your own synthesis or evaluation.

skills.name: Synthesising literature
skills.description: Practical guidance to combine multiple sources around a shared pattern, explanation, or unresolved tension, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Combine multiple sources around a shared pattern, explanation, or unresolved tension.
skills.example: Across qualitative and survey studies, flexible scheduling is consistently associated with greater perceived autonomy.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep each proposition attached to supporting citations, and distinguish source claims from your own synthesis or evaluation.

skills.name: Comparing studies
skills.description: Practical guidance to state a meaningful similarity between studies on a common basis, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: State a meaningful similarity between studies on a common basis.
skills.example: Both studies treat trust as relational, although they operationalise it with different indicators.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep each proposition attached to supporting citations, and distinguish source claims from your own synthesis or evaluation.

skills.name: Contrasting studies
skills.description: Practical guidance to state a meaningful difference between studies and identify the basis of contrast, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: State a meaningful difference between studies and identify the basis of contrast.
skills.example: Whereas the national survey reports gradual change, the case study documents an abrupt local shift after closure.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep each proposition attached to supporting citations, and distinguish source claims from your own synthesis or evaluation.

skills.name: Describing scholarly consensus
skills.description: Practical guidance to represent broad agreement only when the reviewed evidence genuinely converges, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Represent broad agreement only when the reviewed evidence genuinely converges.
skills.example: Reviews generally agree that measurement error can attenuate estimated associations.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep each proposition attached to supporting citations, and distinguish source claims from your own synthesis or evaluation.

skills.name: Describing scholarly disagreement
skills.description: Practical guidance to locate disagreement in assumptions, methods, evidence, or interpretation, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Locate disagreement in assumptions, methods, evidence, or interpretation.
skills.example: Scholars disagree over whether the reform altered incentives or merely formalised practices already in place.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep each proposition attached to supporting citations, and distinguish source claims from your own synthesis or evaluation.

skills.name: Identifying limitations in prior work
skills.description: Practical guidance to describe a constraint in earlier evidence and explain its consequence without dismissing the work, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Describe a constraint in earlier evidence and explain its consequence without dismissing the work.
skills.example: Because earlier samples were drawn from specialist clinics, their estimates may not transfer to community settings.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep each proposition attached to supporting citations, and distinguish source claims from your own synthesis or evaluation.

skills.name: Critiquing previous research
skills.description: Practical guidance to evaluate a specific claim, method, or inference using explicit criteria and evidence, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Evaluate a specific claim, method, or inference using explicit criteria and evidence.
skills.example: The proposed typology is useful descriptively, but its categories overlap when applied to multilingual interviews.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep each proposition attached to supporting citations, and distinguish source claims from your own synthesis or evaluation.

skills.name: Qualifying criticism
skills.description: Practical guidance to acknowledge what prior work establishes before defining a narrower concern, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Acknowledge what prior work establishes before defining a narrower concern.
skills.example: The model offers a clear account of short-term adaptation; however, it does not address changes beyond the first year.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep each proposition attached to supporting citations, and distinguish source claims from your own synthesis or evaluation.

skills.name: Establishing a literature gap
skills.description: Practical guidance to show what the literature does not yet resolve after representing what it already covers, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Show what the literature does not yet resolve after representing what it already covers.
skills.example: Existing reviews catalogue reported barriers but do not compare how those barriers vary by contract type.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep each proposition attached to supporting citations, and distinguish source claims from your own synthesis or evaluation.

skills.name: Writing related work
skills.description: Practical guidance to organise related work by analytical relationship rather than as a sequence of isolated summaries, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Organise related work by analytical relationship rather than as a sequence of isolated summaries.
skills.example: Prior approaches fall into three groups: rule-based extraction, supervised classification, and hybrid retrieval.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep each proposition attached to supporting citations, and distinguish source claims from your own synthesis or evaluation.

skills.name: Transitioning between sources
skills.description: Practical guidance to make the logical relation between one source and the next explicit, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Make the logical relation between one source and the next explicit.
skills.example: This institutional account is extended by later ethnographic work, which shows how the rule is negotiated in practice.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep each proposition attached to supporting citations, and distinguish source claims from your own synthesis or evaluation.

skills.name: Citation-integrated writing
skills.description: Practical guidance to attach attribution to the exact proposition supported by a source, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Attach attribution to the exact proposition supported by a source.
skills.example: Rahman and Lee report that response time declined after triage was reorganised, while noting substantial variation across sites.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep each proposition attached to supporting citations, and distinguish source claims from your own synthesis or evaluation.

skills.name: Making an academic claim
skills.description: Practical guidance to state a contestable proposition with clear scope and an appropriate level of confidence, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: State a contestable proposition with clear scope and an appropriate level of confidence.
skills.example: These findings suggest that access, rather than awareness alone, constrains participation in the programme.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Match assertiveness to the supplied evidence and scope; do not turn an interpretation, association, or example into established fact.

skills.name: Supporting a claim
skills.description: Practical guidance to connect a proposition to the evidence, reasoning, or source that warrants it, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Connect a proposition to the evidence, reasoning, or source that warrants it.
skills.example: This interpretation is supported by the repeated appearance of the same concern across all four interview groups.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Match assertiveness to the supplied evidence and scope; do not turn an interpretation, association, or example into established fact.

skills.name: Qualifying a claim
skills.description: Practical guidance to limit a claim by confidence, population, condition, or analytical perspective, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Limit a claim by confidence, population, condition, or analytical perspective.
skills.example: Within the sampled districts, the pattern appears strongest where public transport is infrequent.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Match assertiveness to the supplied evidence and scope; do not turn an interpretation, association, or example into established fact.

skills.name: Hedging
skills.description: Practical guidance to mark possibility or uncertainty without making the sentence empty or evasive, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Mark possibility or uncertainty without making the sentence empty or evasive.
skills.example: One possible explanation is that participants interpreted the reminder as a signal of institutional support.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Match assertiveness to the supplied evidence and scope; do not turn an interpretation, association, or example into established fact.

skills.name: Emphasising cautiously
skills.description: Practical guidance to signal a well-supported point without implying certainty beyond the evidence, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Signal a well-supported point without implying certainty beyond the evidence.
skills.example: Notably, the difference remained similar across all prespecified sensitivity checks.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Match assertiveness to the supplied evidence and scope; do not turn an interpretation, association, or example into established fact.

skills.name: Conceding a point
skills.description: Practical guidance to acknowledge a valid counterpoint before clarifying its effect on the argument, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Acknowledge a valid counterpoint before clarifying its effect on the argument.
skills.example: Although cost is an important constraint, it does not fully explain why uptake differs between adjacent districts.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Match assertiveness to the supplied evidence and scope; do not turn an interpretation, association, or example into established fact.

skills.name: Presenting counterarguments
skills.description: Practical guidance to represent a plausible opposing position fairly before evaluating it, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Represent a plausible opposing position fairly before evaluating it.
skills.example: An alternative view is that the observed change reflects seasonal demand rather than the new scheduling policy.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Match assertiveness to the supplied evidence and scope; do not turn an interpretation, association, or example into established fact.

skills.name: Drawing distinctions
skills.description: Practical guidance to separate concepts, mechanisms, populations, or levels of analysis that should not be conflated, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Separate concepts, mechanisms, populations, or levels of analysis that should not be conflated.
skills.example: Administrative compliance should be distinguished from substantive adoption of the policy.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Match assertiveness to the supplied evidence and scope; do not turn an interpretation, association, or example into established fact.

skills.name: Expressing agreement
skills.description: Practical guidance to align with another account while specifying the proposition being endorsed, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Align with another account while specifying the proposition being endorsed.
skills.example: This analysis supports Morgan's distinction between procedural access and practical availability.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Match assertiveness to the supplied evidence and scope; do not turn an interpretation, association, or example into established fact.

skills.name: Expressing disagreement
skills.description: Practical guidance to challenge a proposition precisely without overstating what the present evidence disproves, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Challenge a proposition precisely without overstating what the present evidence disproves.
skills.example: Our results do not support the claim that the two indicators are interchangeable in low-resource settings.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Match assertiveness to the supplied evidence and scope; do not turn an interpretation, association, or example into established fact.

skills.name: Defining concepts
skills.description: Practical guidance to give a working meaning that establishes how a term is used in the argument, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Give a working meaning that establishes how a term is used in the argument.
skills.example: Here, resilience refers to the capacity to maintain essential services during and immediately after disruption.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Match assertiveness to the supplied evidence and scope; do not turn an interpretation, association, or example into established fact.

skills.name: Classifying concepts
skills.description: Practical guidance to organise cases into explicit categories using a stated principle, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Organise cases into explicit categories using a stated principle.
skills.example: We classify responses as anticipatory, reactive, or restorative according to when action begins.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Match assertiveness to the supplied evidence and scope; do not turn an interpretation, association, or example into established fact.

skills.name: Giving examples
skills.description: Practical guidance to illustrate an abstract point with a representative case without treating the example as proof by itself, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Illustrate an abstract point with a representative case without treating the example as proof by itself.
skills.example: For example, a library may expand access by offering evening hours rather than by opening a new branch.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Match assertiveness to the supplied evidence and scope; do not turn an interpretation, association, or example into established fact.

skills.name: Drawing comparisons
skills.description: Practical guidance to compare entities on a named dimension and hold the basis of comparison constant, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Compare entities on a named dimension and hold the basis of comparison constant.
skills.example: Compared with fixed grants, matching funds place more of the short-term financing risk on local organisations.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Match assertiveness to the supplied evidence and scope; do not turn an interpretation, association, or example into established fact.

skills.name: Explaining implications
skills.description: Practical guidance to state what a finding or argument changes for theory, method, practice, or further inquiry, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: State what a finding or argument changes for theory, method, practice, or further inquiry.
skills.example: The result implies that evaluations should measure service continuity as well as initial deployment.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Match assertiveness to the supplied evidence and scope; do not turn an interpretation, association, or example into established fact.

skills.name: Thesis introduction
skills.description: Practical guidance to open the thesis by connecting context, problem, aim, approach, and contribution, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Open the thesis by connecting context, problem, aim, approach, and contribution.
skills.example: This thesis investigates how coastal households adapt water use during recurring dry seasons.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep chapter-level claims consistent with the thesis evidence; summaries and conclusions must not introduce unsupported results.

skills.name: Chapter introduction
skills.description: Practical guidance to preview a chapter's purpose, scope, and relationship to the wider thesis, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Preview a chapter's purpose, scope, and relationship to the wider thesis.
skills.example: This chapter develops the conceptual basis for the comparative analysis presented in Chapters Four and Five.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep chapter-level claims consistent with the thesis evidence; summaries and conclusions must not introduce unsupported results.

skills.name: Literature review
skills.description: Practical guidance to build a critical synthesis that establishes the study's scholarly position, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Build a critical synthesis that establishes the study's scholarly position.
skills.example: Taken together, the literature explains adoption decisions well but offers less insight into long-term maintenance.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep chapter-level claims consistent with the thesis evidence; summaries and conclusions must not introduce unsupported results.

skills.name: Conceptual framework
skills.description: Practical guidance to define the concepts and relationships that guide data collection or interpretation, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Define the concepts and relationships that guide data collection or interpretation.
skills.example: The framework distinguishes resource access, practical capability, and realised participation.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep chapter-level claims consistent with the thesis evidence; summaries and conclusions must not introduce unsupported results.

skills.name: Theoretical framework
skills.description: Practical guidance to explain which theory guides the analysis and why it fits the research problem, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Explain which theory guides the analysis and why it fits the research problem.
skills.example: Institutional theory is used here to examine how formal rules and local routines interact over time.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep chapter-level claims consistent with the thesis evidence; summaries and conclusions must not introduce unsupported results.

skills.name: Methodology chapter
skills.description: Practical guidance to explain and justify the overall research design, epistemic choices, and procedures, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Explain and justify the overall research design, epistemic choices, and procedures.
skills.example: A comparative case design was selected to examine how the same regulation operates in contrasting administrative settings.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep chapter-level claims consistent with the thesis evidence; summaries and conclusions must not introduce unsupported results.

skills.name: Findings chapter
skills.description: Practical guidance to present analysed evidence in an ordered structure without importing unsupported interpretation, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Present analysed evidence in an ordered structure without importing unsupported interpretation.
skills.example: Three recurring patterns were identified: delayed access, informal substitution, and partial recovery.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep chapter-level claims consistent with the thesis evidence; summaries and conclusions must not introduce unsupported results.

skills.name: Discussion chapter
skills.description: Practical guidance to interpret findings in relation to questions, literature, theory, and design limits, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Interpret findings in relation to questions, literature, theory, and design limits.
skills.example: The findings refine earlier accounts by showing that capacity varies not only between organisations but also across project stages.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep chapter-level claims consistent with the thesis evidence; summaries and conclusions must not introduce unsupported results.

skills.name: Chapter summary
skills.description: Practical guidance to close a chapter by consolidating its result and preparing the next analytical step, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Close a chapter by consolidating its result and preparing the next analytical step.
skills.example: This chapter established the measurement model; the next chapter evaluates its performance across sites.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep chapter-level claims consistent with the thesis evidence; summaries and conclusions must not introduce unsupported results.

skills.name: General conclusion
skills.description: Practical guidance to synthesize the thesis's answer and contribution without introducing new evidence, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Synthesize the thesis's answer and contribution without introducing new evidence.
skills.example: Overall, the thesis shows that continuity depends on coordination across technical and institutional boundaries.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep chapter-level claims consistent with the thesis evidence; summaries and conclusions must not introduce unsupported results.

skills.name: Recommendations
skills.description: Practical guidance to derive bounded actions from the study's findings, audience, and constraints, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Derive bounded actions from the study's findings, audience, and constraints.
skills.example: Universities could pilot the advising model in one faculty before considering wider implementation.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep chapter-level claims consistent with the thesis evidence; summaries and conclusions must not introduce unsupported results.

skills.name: Future research
skills.description: Practical guidance to identify a consequential unresolved question that follows from the study, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Identify a consequential unresolved question that follows from the study.
skills.example: Future studies should test whether the observed pattern persists beyond the first two years of implementation.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep chapter-level claims consistent with the thesis evidence; summaries and conclusions must not introduce unsupported results.

skills.name: Thesis limitations
skills.description: Practical guidance to explain how design or evidence constraints bound the thesis's conclusions, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Explain how design or evidence constraints bound the thesis's conclusions.
skills.example: Because the archive is incomplete before 1980, the thesis cannot determine when the shift first began.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Keep chapter-level claims consistent with the thesis evidence; summaries and conclusions must not introduce unsupported results.

skills.name: Academic abstract
skills.description: Practical guidance to condense the problem, approach, principal result, and bounded conclusion into a self-contained summary, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Condense the problem, approach, principal result, and bounded conclusion into a self-contained summary.
skills.example: Using panel data from 42 districts, we estimate changes in clinic attendance and find substantial variation by travel time.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Report submission, contribution, ethics, availability, and disclosure facts exactly; do not use promotional language as evidence.

skills.name: Research proposal
skills.description: Practical guidance to present a feasible question, rationale, design, and expected contribution before evidence is collected, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Present a feasible question, rationale, design, and expected contribution before evidence is collected.
skills.example: The proposed study will compare two onboarding models using prespecified retention and accessibility outcomes.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Report submission, contribution, ethics, availability, and disclosure facts exactly; do not use promotional language as evidence.

skills.name: Journal manuscript
skills.description: Practical guidance to coordinate the full research argument for a journal audience and reporting convention, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Coordinate the full research argument for a journal audience and reporting convention.
skills.example: The manuscript first defines the policy change, then evaluates implementation and interprets variation across regions.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Report submission, contribution, ethics, availability, and disclosure facts exactly; do not use promotional language as evidence.

skills.name: Conference paper
skills.description: Practical guidance to focus a research report around one clear contribution suitable for a time-limited presentation, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Focus a research report around one clear contribution suitable for a time-limited presentation.
skills.example: This paper reports the evaluation design and the first six months of implementation evidence.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Report submission, contribution, ethics, availability, and disclosure facts exactly; do not use promotional language as evidence.

skills.name: Cover letter
skills.description: Practical guidance to explain a submission's fit and contribution to an editor without inflated promotional claims, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Explain a submission's fit and contribution to an editor without inflated promotional claims.
skills.example: We submit this manuscript because its comparison of open-source audit methods aligns with the journal's focus on reproducible evaluation.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Report submission, contribution, ethics, availability, and disclosure facts exactly; do not use promotional language as evidence.

skills.name: Reviewer response
skills.description: Practical guidance to answer each review point with a revision, evidence-based explanation, or respectful rationale, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Answer each review point with a revision, evidence-based explanation, or respectful rationale.
skills.example: We agree that the sampling description was incomplete and have added the recruitment dates and exclusion process on page 8.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Report submission, contribution, ethics, availability, and disclosure facts exactly; do not use promotional language as evidence.

skills.name: Revision response
skills.description: Practical guidance to document exactly what changed and where, while distinguishing revisions from unresolved disagreements, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Document exactly what changed and where, while distinguishing revisions from unresolved disagreements.
skills.example: We revised Figure 2, added the requested uncertainty intervals, and clarified the remaining data limitation in Section 4.3.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Report submission, contribution, ethics, availability, and disclosure facts exactly; do not use promotional language as evidence.

skills.name: Author contribution statement
skills.description: Practical guidance to attribute research roles transparently using the publication's required vocabulary, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Attribute research roles transparently using the publication's required vocabulary.

skills.name: Causal language
skills.description: Practical guidance to reserve causal wording for a design and analysis that identify the stated intervention or exposure effect, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Reserve causal wording for a design and analysis that identify the stated intervention or exposure effect.
skills.example: Random assignment supports the conclusion that the reminder increased appointment attendance in this trial.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Causal verbs require a credible causal design; association, prediction, significance, and null results do not establish causation.

skills.name: Evidence strength
skills.description: Practical guidance to calibrate wording to relevance, directness, precision, consistency, and design quality, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Calibrate wording to relevance, directness, precision, consistency, and design quality.
skills.example: The converging laboratory and field results provide moderate support for the proposed degradation pathway.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Causal verbs require a credible causal design; association, prediction, significance, and null results do not establish causation.

skills.name: Hedging scientific claims
skills.description: Practical guidance to use precise uncertainty markers that identify what is possible, estimated, or not resolved, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Use precise uncertainty markers that identify what is possible, estimated, or not resolved.
skills.example: The observed pattern may reflect a threshold response, although gradual change cannot be excluded.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Causal verbs require a credible causal design; association, prediction, significance, and null results do not establish causation.

skills.name: Avoiding overclaiming
skills.description: Practical guidance to remove claims of proof, universality, or importance that the evidence does not warrant, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Remove claims of proof, universality, or importance that the evidence does not warrant.
skills.example: The data support improved short-term detection, not the claim that the method is universally superior.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Causal verbs require a credible causal design; association, prediction, significance, and null results do not establish causation.

skills.name: Interpreting null results
skills.description: Practical guidance to separate failure to detect a clear effect from evidence of equivalence or absence, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Separate failure to detect a clear effect from evidence of equivalence or absence.
skills.example: The non-significant estimate is inconclusive because the interval includes effects in both directions.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Causal verbs require a credible causal design; association, prediction, significance, and null results do not establish causation.

skills.name: Effect size language
skills.description: Practical guidance to describe magnitude on an interpretable scale and distinguish it from statistical significance, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Describe magnitude on an interpretable scale and distinguish it from statistical significance.
skills.example: The intervention changed the mean score by 0.18 standard deviations, a small effect on the prespecified scale.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Causal verbs require a credible causal design; association, prediction, significance, and null results do not establish causation.

skills.name: Uncertainty language
skills.description: Practical guidance to attach uncertainty to the exact estimate, inference, or explanation it qualifies, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Attach uncertainty to the exact estimate, inference, or explanation it qualifies.
skills.example: The point estimate favours treatment, but substantial benefit and no effect are both compatible with the interval.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Causal verbs require a credible causal design; association, prediction, significance, and null results do not establish causation.

skills.name: Scope and generalisation
skills.description: Practical guidance to limit conclusions to populations, settings, outcomes, and time horizons supported by the study, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Limit conclusions to populations, settings, outcomes, and time horizons supported by the study.
skills.example: These results concern supervised laboratory operation and should not be generalised to unattended field deployment.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Causal verbs require a credible causal design; association, prediction, significance, and null results do not establish causation.

skills.name: Meaning-preserving paraphrase
skills.description: Practical guidance to restate a passage in independent language while preserving its propositions, scope, and attribution, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Restate a passage in independent language while preserving its propositions, scope, and attribution.
skills.example: Source: The intervention produced a modest decline in waiting time. Rewrite: Waiting time decreased modestly following the intervention.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Preserve attribution, meaning, numbers, negation, scope, and claim strength; paraphrasing never removes citation duties.

skills.name: Structural paraphrase
skills.description: Practical guidance to change clause structure and information order rather than substituting isolated synonyms, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Change clause structure and information order rather than substituting isolated synonyms.
skills.example: Source: Because rainfall was limited, crop yields declined. Rewrite: Limited rainfall was accompanied by lower crop yields.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Preserve attribution, meaning, numbers, negation, scope, and claim strength; paraphrasing never removes citation duties.

skills.name: Academic paraphrase
skills.description: Practical guidance to restate source-dependent academic prose clearly without erasing citation responsibility, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Restate source-dependent academic prose clearly without erasing citation responsibility.
skills.example: Source: Patel argues that informal rules shape access. Rewrite: Access is shaped by informal rules, according to Patel.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Preserve attribution, meaning, numbers, negation, scope, and claim strength; paraphrasing never removes citation duties.

skills.name: Scientific paraphrase
skills.description: Practical guidance to rewrite scientific prose while preserving design, quantities, uncertainty, and inferential level, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Rewrite scientific prose while preserving design, quantities, uncertainty, and inferential level.
skills.example: Source: The groups differed by 3.1 units, with wide uncertainty. Rewrite: The estimated between-group difference was 3.1 units, although precision was low.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Preserve attribution, meaning, numbers, negation, scope, and claim strength; paraphrasing never removes citation duties.

skills.name: Concision
skills.description: Practical guidance to remove expendable wording while retaining every proposition needed by the argument, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Remove expendable wording while retaining every proposition needed by the argument.
skills.example: Before: It is important to note that the two groups were similar. After: The two groups were similar.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Preserve attribution, meaning, numbers, negation, scope, and claim strength; paraphrasing never removes citation duties.

skills.name: Sentence restructuring
skills.description: Practical guidance to split, combine, or reorder clauses to improve comprehension without changing logical relations, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Split, combine, or reorder clauses to improve comprehension without changing logical relations.
skills.example: Before: The model was accurate, but because calibration was poor, deployment was delayed. After: Deployment was delayed because calibration was poor, despite the model's accuracy.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Preserve attribution, meaning, numbers, negation, scope, and claim strength; paraphrasing never removes citation duties.

skills.name: Citation-preserving rewrite
skills.description: Practical guidance to keep citations attached to the propositions they support throughout a rewrite, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Keep citations attached to the propositions they support throughout a rewrite.
skills.example: Source: Early access improves retention (Diaz, 2024). Rewrite: Diaz (2024) links earlier access with improved retention.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Preserve attribution, meaning, numbers, negation, scope, and claim strength; paraphrasing never removes citation duties.

skills.name: Number-preserving rewrite
skills.description: Practical guidance to preserve values, units, denominators, directions, and statistical qualifiers exactly, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Preserve values, units, denominators, directions, and statistical qualifiers exactly.
skills.example: Source: Error fell from 12% to 9%. Rewrite: The error rate decreased by 3 percentage points, from 12% to 9%.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Preserve attribution, meaning, numbers, negation, scope, and claim strength; paraphrasing never removes citation duties.

skills.name: Claim-strength-preserving rewrite
skills.description: Practical guidance to keep tentative, bounded, assertive, and causal force unchanged unless evidence is reassessed, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Keep tentative, bounded, assertive, and causal force unchanged unless evidence is reassessed.
skills.example: Source: The pattern may indicate delayed adaptation. Rewrite: Delayed adaptation is one possible interpretation of the pattern.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Preserve attribution, meaning, numbers, negation, scope, and claim strength; paraphrasing never removes citation duties.

skills.name: Cautious rewriting
skills.description: Practical guidance to reduce unjustified certainty by naming limits while retaining the useful proposition, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Reduce unjustified certainty by naming limits while retaining the useful proposition.
skills.example: Before: The programme solved the access problem. After: The programme was associated with improved access during the study period.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Preserve attribution, meaning, numbers, negation, scope, and claim strength; paraphrasing never removes citation duties.

skills.name: Academic register
skills.description: Practical guidance to replace conversational or inflated wording with precise, readable scholarly language, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Replace conversational or inflated wording with precise, readable scholarly language.
skills.example: Before: The results are super convincing. After: The results provide consistent support for the proposed explanation.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Preserve attribution, meaning, numbers, negation, scope, and claim strength; paraphrasing never removes citation duties.

skills.name: Removing unnecessary verbosity
skills.description: Practical guidance to delete metadiscourse and repetition that do not change meaning or guide the reader, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Delete metadiscourse and repetition that do not change meaning or guide the reader.
skills.example: Before: It should be pointed out that costs increased. After: Costs increased.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Preserve attribution, meaning, numbers, negation, scope, and claim strength; paraphrasing never removes citation duties.

skills.name: Reducing repetition
skills.description: Practical guidance to vary sentence structure or consolidate repeated propositions without introducing new claims, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Vary sentence structure or consolidate repeated propositions without introducing new claims.
skills.example: Before: Access improved. Access improved most in rural sites. After: Access improved, especially in rural sites.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Preserve attribution, meaning, numbers, negation, scope, and claim strength; paraphrasing never removes citation duties.

skills.name: Improving logical flow
skills.description: Practical guidance to make relations among propositions explicit through order, reference, and appropriate linkage, with wording aligned to rhetorical purpose and available evidence.
skills.rhetorical_objective: Make relations among propositions explicit through order, reference, and appropriate linkage.
skills.example: Before: Uptake fell. Support ended. The timing matters. After: Uptake fell after support ended, making the timing relevant to interpretation.
skills.evidence_claim_warning: Preserve attribution, meaning, numbers, negation, scope, and claim strength; paraphrasing never removes citation duties.
